solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Remnant is substandard, needing price reduction

parts.note: food or a performance that is off has gone bad or below par
a cut is a reduction in price

explanation.surface: A leftover piece of cloth is poor quality and must be marked down.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece trimmed away and left over from a larger sheet or length is a remnant.

clue.text: Visual changes to the Capitol

indicators.note: the letters of the building's name are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Alterations made to the look of the Capitol building in Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe things relating to sight or the eye.

clue.text: Strange forenames of the lodger?

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of the next word appear in an odd arrangement

explanation.surface: Odd first names belonging to the person renting a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lodger' looks like a tenant, but here it is a playful coinage for a member of a Masonic lodge, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons meet in lodges, so one could whimsically be called a lodge member or lodger.

clue.text: Outcome of an anti-aircraft gun?

definitions.meaning: such a gun fires its shot upward, read as two words

explanation.surface: Asking what the result of using an anti-aircraft weapon is.
explanation.definitionFit: The result or eventual consequence of something is its upshot.

clue.text: Engage in competition without money to finish

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the competing word goes round the money

parts.note: to compete is to engage in competition
L stands for pound, the British unit of money (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Taking part in a contest with no cash, right to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but it means outside: COMPETE wraps L.
explanation.definitionFit: To complete something is to bring it to its end, a synonym of finish.

clue.text: Love girl's curved shape

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, written as the letter O
Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie

explanation.surface: A girl's beloved rounded figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg-like rounded outline is a curved shape.

clue.text: A long time in short trousers and spectacles

indicators.note: in places the long time within the trousers

parts.note: pants are short underpants or, in the US, trousers; short here hints at shorts
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Someone spent ages wearing shorts and glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spectacles' looks like glasses, but means grand public shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate public shows with costumed processions are spectacles.

clue.text: Type out a note in a foreign country

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their usual order

parts.note: G is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: Typing out a memo while working abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a country, foreign to a British solver, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Comes out east and joins up

parts.note: to merge is to join together

explanation.surface: Something appears in the east and unites with others.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out into view.

clue.text: Convert me with this belief

indicators.note: convert is to change something into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A preacher urging a listener to adopt their creed.
explanation.definitionFit: Belief in a god or gods is the doctrine named here.

clue.text: It drains off water from scrambled Royal egg

indicators.note: scrambled, as of eggs, means mixed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Water runs off a scrambled egg fit for royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved stone spout on a church roof throws rainwater away from the walls.

clue.text: They don't have a quiet retirement

definitions.text: They don't have a quiet retirement

parts.words: They don't have a quiet retirement
parts.note: retirement here is going to bed, not stopping work; noisy sleepers make it unquiet

explanation.surface: Pensioners who lead a busy life after leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: People who breathe noisily in sleep make their night's rest anything but quiet.

clue.text: Add on to a POW camp

definitions.meaning: to make worse or greater by adding, as interest builds on interest
an enclosed area where prisoners of war are held

explanation.surface: Appending something to a prison camp for captured soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to intensify by adding and an enclosure such as a prison camp.

clue.text: Cheap newspaper with stock phrase for the riff-raff

parts.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper
a tag is a familiar saying or catchphrase

explanation.surface: A tabloid using clichés aimed at the lower orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A disreputable mixed crowd of people is the rabble or riff-raff.

clue.text: It's customary for escort to leave assault course when injured

indicators.note: the letters of the companion word are to go out of the mixture
injured suggests damage, so the letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A minder quits an army training run after getting hurt, which is normal.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix ASSAULT COURSE, take away the letters of ESCORT, and rearrange the remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the normal, customary way.

clue.text: Pay attention or bend over

definitions.meaning: an archaic sense meaning to listen
a ship that leans to one side is said to do this

explanation.surface: An instruction to listen or to stoop.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means archaically to listen, and also to lean or tilt over.

clue.text: Brazen supporters that really mean business

parts.note: brass is impudence or cheek, and brazen means made of brass
tacks are small nails that hold things in place

explanation.surface: Shameless backers who are serious about trade.
explanation.walkthrough: To get down to brass tacks is to deal with the essentials, which is to really mean business.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for essentials is used of people who are serious and practical.

clue.text: Aplomb of company representative certain about nothing

indicators.note: about means round, so the pair of words surround the nothing

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative
sure means certain
nothing is zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A confident firm's spokesperson sure about nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm self-assurance under pressure is aplomb.

clue.text: Pennant flown by vessel with monarch aboard

indicators.note: aboard puts the monarch on board the ship

parts.note: a steamer is a steamship, a vessel
R stands for Rex or Regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A flag flies from a ship carrying a king.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow flag flown from a mast is a streamer.

clue.text: A way to regulate the economy from Roman times

definitions.text: A way to regulate the economy

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is made out of the letters that follow, reworked

explanation.surface: An economic policy that dates back to ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' looks like it gives a date or origin, but it signals the letters of ROMAN TIMES rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Control of the money supply as the main means of managing an economy is this doctrine.

clue.text: No terms could describe such a wicked person

indicators.note: the letters can be arranged to trace out the answer, as if describing it

explanation.surface: Words fail to portray someone so evil.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruel, wicked person is called an ogre or brute.

clue.text: Large number seen in a doctor's rounds

indicators.note: seen in places the large number inside the other pieces

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
M is 1000 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Many patients visited by a doctor on hospital rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' looks like a doctor's ward visits, but means bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammunition is counted in rounds, each a single cartridge.

clue.text: Have an ambition that gives advantage to opponents

parts.note: to own is to have
a goal is an ambition or aim

explanation.surface: Having aspirations that end up helping your rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoring into your own net gives the other side a free point.

clue.text: Highballs for winter sportsmen

definitions.meaning: high kicks or hits in rugby or cricket, not drinks
people who travel downhill over snow on long runners

explanation.surface: Cocktails for people on a winter holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both balls hit high into the air and people who ski.

clue.text: Built a home for a good man in want

indicators.note: in places the good man inside the want

parts.note: need means want or lack
ST is saint, a good man

explanation.surface: A house built for a decent person who is poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'want' looks like a desire, but means need.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds that have built a nest have made themselves a home.

clue.text: Deserted area is in a poor state

indicators.note: a poor state is a mess, so the letters are put in disorder

explanation.surface: An empty region left in an impoverished country.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula between Africa and Asia is largely desert.

clue.text: Finance advanced for riverside development

definitions.meaning: humorously, building on the edge of a river

explanation.surface: Money put up for a riverside housing project.
explanation.definitionFit: Money lent by a lender is called this, and a river edge is a bank.

clue.text: She was a copper, once, in India

definitions.text: She was a copper, once, in India

parts.words: She was a copper, once, in India
parts.note: not a policewoman: a former copper coin of India, which is also a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman who served as a police officer in India.
explanation.definitionFit: An old Indian coin worth a sixteenth of a rupee, and also a woman's name.

clue.text: Holding belief about humanity

indicators.note: about means around, so the belief surrounds the humanity

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief
men stands for people in general

explanation.surface: A conviction regarding the human race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: property held, such as a block of flats.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a holding of land or property held by tenure is a tenement.

clue.text: It's held musically to follow the wrong tune

indicators.note: follow places the small word after the reworked tune
the tune is put wrong, its letters out of order

explanation.surface: Someone sings the wrong melody, holding a note.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction to sustain a note for its full value.

clue.text: Force both sides into a radio broadcast

indicators.note: into puts the two sides inside the rearranged letters
broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread out anew

parts.note: left and right, L and R

explanation.surface: Pushing both parties onto a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' is the verb, to push something through quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To pressure someone into acting hastily is to force them.

clue.text: It follows a gale at sea, too

definitions.text: It follows a gale at sea
definitions.meaning: a rolling sea follows a storm, read as two words

explanation.surface: Something comes after a storm at sea, in addition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in addition, a synonym of also.
